problem: Prior VLM-based zero-shot ObjectNav methods use VLMs only as passive CLIP/BLIP-style similarity scorers. They have no memory of past decisions, so they oscillate or loop in ambiguous places such as identical corridors and doorways.
motivation: ObjectNav needs semantic reasoning about where objects are likely to be, but current systems barely use VLM reasoning ability. The authors observed that memoryless VLM guidance produces contradictory suggestions and decision loops, so they add temporal context to the prompt.
key_idea: Prompt an open-source VLM (LLaVA-1.6-7B) with the target and the last N actions to output action probability scores that are projected into a frontier-exploration value map, and add VLM-verified, segmentation-based supplementary waypoints for the final approach.
insight: Action history in the prompt gives a small gain: removing it drops SR from 46 to 44 and SPL from 24.8 to 23.7, which is evidence of reduced oscillation but not strong evidence. Evaluation is on only 50 episodes, so a 2-point SR difference is one episode and lies within noise. The paper also finds the VLM is sometimes inconsistent with its own scene interpretation, and that instance-level ground truth penalizes finding another valid instance of the target class.
method: Frontier exploration: builds a 2D top-down obstacle map from depth, takes frontier midpoints as candidate waypoints, and navigates with a VER low-level policy pretrained on PointNav.
VLM action scoring: LLaVA-1.6-7B looks at the egocentric RGB with the target name and outputs 0-1 scores for forward/backward/left/right using a strict output template.

Value map with uncertainty: projects scores onto the map with confidence c=exp(-λd)·cos²(θ/(fov/2)·π/2) and fuses re-observations by confidence-weighted averaging. The agent goes to the frontier with the highest value.

Action history prompting: the prompt includes the last N (e.g. 10) actions plus instructions to avoid contradictory or repetitive actions, with a fallback that repeats the last valid non-turn action on persistent oscillation.
Detection and verification: YOLOv7 (COCO classes) and Grounding-DINO (open-vocabulary) detect the target at confidence >0.8, and the VLM then verifies the detection.
Supplementary waypoints: Mobile-SAM segments the verified object, KNN clustering on pixels with value >0.8 gives cluster-center waypoints, and these are fed to VER for the final approach.

setting.backbone: LLaVA-1.6 7B (frozen) for guidance; VER (pretrained PointNav policy) for low-level control; YOLOv7 / Grounding-DINO detectors; Mobile-SAM
setting.action_space: discrete: move forward 0.25 m, turn left/right 30°, stop (look up/down unused)

numbers.eval_set_note: 50 episodes selected from the full validation set
numbers.extra: action history N=10; 500 step limit; 1 m success radius

numbers_note: Only a 50-episode subset was evaluated; baseline numbers in Table I are copied from their papers on the full split, so the comparison is not like-for-like.
results: The method reaches 46% SR and 24.8% SPL on a 50-episode HM3D ObjectNav validation subset. This is below VLFM (52.5 SR / 30.4 SPL) and GAMap (53.1 SR), and above FBE (33.7/15.3) and PixNav (37.9/20.5). Removing action history lowers SR to 44 and SPL to 23.7.
limitations: Evaluated on only 50 episodes, so the results and the ablation are statistically weak, and SR is below the strongest baselines despite the 'comparable' claim.
VLM inference at every frame is computationally heavy, so real-time use is hard, and the VLM sometimes gives recommendations inconsistent with its own scene understanding.
Only simulation results; only the action-history ablation is reported, with no ablation of the waypoint refinement or the value map.
